doc: Design tokens every library component reads. Each colour has a light and a dark value; the expansion writes it as a themed colour ({light, dark} in resources.colors), which the player picks by the system theme. A document overrides a colour by defining it in resources.colors (same name), with one value for both modes or its own {light, dark}; colours stay named in the .rc, so a host can re-theme at run time too. Numbers are substituted when components expand. `modes` holds the mono palettes: mono (light on black, for always-on displays) and mono-inverted (dark on white, for e-ink and other reflective displays). By default (componentTheme "auto") one document serves every look: light and dark by the system theme, mono and mono-inverted when the host sets the exported float theme.mono to 1 and overrides the named colours with that palette (components keep both variants, gated by theme.mono at run time). componentTheme "light", "dark", "light-dark", "mono" or "mono-inverted" expands one look only, smaller. monoOutline is transparent in light and dark and the outline in mono: a ring a mono surface draws instead of its fill, with the same structure in every look; monoBackground, transparent too, is the background in mono: the hole of a ring (Avatar)

light.doc: Only the light values, as plain colours: no themed-colour ops, for a document that is always light.

dark.doc: Only the dark values, as plain colours (the library's look before themed colours).

mono.doc: Black, white and one grey, light on black: for always-on displays and OLED (mostly black, thin strokes, few lit pixels), with no animation and no continuous repaint. mono-inverted is the same look dark on white, for e-ink. @theme.mono is 1: components draw their mono variant, with state shown by shape (outlined or filled, a tick, the thumb's side) instead of colour.

mono-inverted.doc: The mono palette inverted, for reflective displays (e-ink, memory LCD) and print: white paper, black text and strokes, and one grey (#616161, 6.2:1 on white, for muted text, outlines, tracks and disabled). The same mono variants (@theme.mono is 1) and no motion. Mono's 'few lit pixels' becomes 'little ink': the same outlined surfaces, now black rings on white.
